summary: Validated with validate --run <run> --submission update44.json returning valid=true. This record surfaces contrary evidence against the documentation anchor I added one turn earlier. Reading the same document's terminology section shows it defines a log entry as committed once the leader that created it has replicated it on a majority of the peers (docs/README.md:21-30), while the implementation computes that majority over voters only and is right to do so, since non-voters are excluded from commitment by definition. So the document uses the peer and voter terms loosely at least once, and the verification line stating that VerifyLeader sends a heartbeat to all voters is best read as intent about the audience of the heartbeat rather than a precise contract. The correction is attached to the knowledge entry I added last turn, so that entry no longer overstates what the documentation establishes; the earlier statement's content about the code paths is unaffected. A successor interpretation for the same question keeps the judgement conditional and unchanged in substance: the code-level contrast still stands, because the threshold is computed from voters while acknowledgements are accepted from every registered peer, and the only way a voter majority can be satisfied by non-voter acknowledgements is the one recorded; the severity still depends on the timing window and configuration already stated, with the lease check remaining an independent voter-based mechanism. Counterevidence kept explicit: the imprecision found runs in the opposite direction from the verification line, so it does not show that sentence to be wrong, only that the document's terminology is unreliable as a contract; and nothing was executed, since this run had no experiment capacity at any point during my work. No stop declaration is made, as budget expiry is a controller boundary.
